DiallelAnalysisR: Diallel Analysis, Heterosis and Related Mating Designs

Source: R/DiallelAnalysisR-package.R
DiallelAnalysisR-package.Rd

DiallelAnalysisR analyses diallel crosses of plant-breeding experiments laid out in randomized complete blocks: Griffing's (1956) four methods and two models, Hayman's (1954) analysis with the \(W_r\)-\(V_r\) graph and the components of variation, the partial diallel between two groups of parents, heterosis, Gardner and Eberhart's models, line by tester and North Carolina designs, diallels over environments, simulation and planning, tables for papers and an interactive application.

Details

Functions.

  • Griffing: combining-ability analysis by Griffing's Methods 1 to 4 and Models 1 (fixed) and 2 (random): analysis of variance, gca, sca and reciprocal effects with standard errors, variance components.

  • Hayman: Hayman's analysis of variance, the \(W_r\)-\(V_r\) analysis and graph, the components \(D\), \(H_1\), \(H_2\), \(F\), \(h^2\), \(E\), genetic ratios and tests of the additive-dominance model.

  • PartialDiallel: crosses between two groups of parents: gca of each group, sca, variance components.

  • GriffingMeans: Griffing's analysis of a table of cross means; GriffingEnv: over several environments.

  • Heterosis: mid-parent, better-parent and standard heterosis with \(t\) tests.

  • GardnerEberhart: Gardner and Eberhart's Analyses II and III.

  • LineTester, NCDesign: line by tester analysis; North Carolina designs I to III.

  • DiallelSim, DiallelPower: simulated diallels and the power of the tests.

  • da_export: the main tables in Word, LaTeX, HTML, Markdown or CSV; DiallelApp: the interactive application.

Every analysis returns the named list documented on its help page, with a class and the methods print, summary, plot and as.data.table; see da-methods. Utilities: da_theme, da_save, da_notation, da_reference.

Data. GriffingData1 (complete diallel of eight parents), its subsets GriffingData2, GriffingData3, GriffingData4 for Methods 2 to 4, HaymanData, PartialDiallelData (ten by four parents), Griffing56 (Griffing's 1956 maize example), LineTesterData and NCData.

Vignettes. Start with vignette("DiallelAnalysisR_01_getting_started", package = "DiallelAnalysisR"); browseVignettes("DiallelAnalysisR") lists all of them, each as HTML and as PDF.

Notation

Scalars are upper-case letters in normal face, indices lower-case italic, vectors lower-case bold and matrices upper-case bold; elements of vectors and matrices keep their letter in normal face. The full table is da_notation().

\(P\), \(B\)number of parents, number of replicates (blocks)
\(i\), \(j\)female and male parent of a cross
\(\mathbf{Y}\), \(Y_{ij}\)matrix of cell means, mean of cross \(i \times j\)
\(\mathbf{g}\), \(g_i\)vector of gca effects, gca effect of parent \(i\)
\(\mathbf{S}\), \(\mathbf{R}\)matrices of sca and reciprocal effects
\(\sigma^2_g\), \(\sigma^2_s\), \(\sigma^2_r\)variances of gca, sca and reciprocal effects (random model)
\(MS_E\), \(\sigma^2_m\)error mean square, error variance of a cell mean
\(V_r\), \(W_r\)variance of array \(r\), its covariance with the parents
\(D\), \(H_1\), \(H_2\), \(F\)Hayman's components of variation

References

Griffing, B. (1956). Concept of general and specific combining ability in relation to diallel crossing systems. Australian Journal of Biological Sciences, 9(4), 463–493. doi:10.1071/BI9560463

Hayman, B. I. (1954). The theory and analysis of diallel crosses. Genetics, 39(6), 789–809. doi:10.1093/genetics/39.6.789

Hayman, B. I. (1954). The analysis of variance of diallel tables. Biometrics, 10(2), 235–244. doi:10.2307/3001877

Kempthorne, O. and Curnow, R. N. (1961). The partial diallel cross. Biometrics, 17(2), 229–250. doi:10.2307/2527989

Singh, R. K. and Chaudhary, B. D. (2004). Biometrical Methods in Quantitative Genetic Analysis. Kalyani Publishers, New Delhi.
